licence.quote_le_15_words: No part of this book may be reproduced without written permission from me

licence.grants_our_words: Nothing beyond fair use (a U.S. doctrine; Apollo's clients are UK/EU, where the nearer concept is fair dealing and narrower).
licence.forbids_our_words: Reproducing any part of the book without written permission.

permits_us: names-only — the rule's NAME and its figures as facts ('45–90 characters', '2–3 alphabets') with a pointer to the chapter; the chapter's sentences stay out of node text; ≤15-word quotes rest on fair use/fair dealing, which the notice acknowledges but does not widen
why_our_words: The clearest all-rights-reserved notice among the thirteen, with an email address for permission. Numbers are not expression, so a node can say '45–90 characters' and point; it cannot carry Butterick's prose. R1's finding 6 already treats the figures as the thing worth holding.
cheap_route_to_lift: One email to mb@mbtype.com — the notice invites requests. Price: one email. Note the author's stated economics: the book is reader-funded and he says so on the legal page; a request from a commercial user should expect to be asked to pay.
unproven: Whether the paperback edition (O'Connor's / Thomson Reuters) carries different terms — not fetched; irrelevant unless a node cites the print edition.

pitfalls.what: 'Fair use' on the page is a U.S. doctrine. A UK bank's asset cannot rely on it; UK fair dealing for quotation is narrower and needs acknowledgement. Treat the ≤15-word quote as the ceiling, not a floor.
pitfalls.owner: Dave's counsel — a one-line house rule on quotation length would settle it for every family

pitfalls.what: The figures (45–90, 2–3 alphabets) have no primary study behind them (R1 finding 6). A pointer node inherits that thinness; grade stays PRACTISED.
